---
title: "Know Your Gear"
---

::: {.ao-story}
You came to Basecamp for a companion, and the quartermaster lays out a long table of other things: the companion itself, the armour it wears, and a pile of fittings no one has labelled. The kennel master swore that a good companion needs nothing more than a name. The quartermaster picks the pieces up one at a time and says what each is for. Start with the companion alone, then watch the armour go on.
:::

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will use the words this site relies on (model, harness, skill, MCP, hook, plugin, effort, eval and the context terms below) and say how they fit together.
- **Before you start:** [Three Kinds of Machine](three-kinds-of-machine.html).
- **Time:** about 15 minutes.
:::

People mix these words up, and the mix-ups cause real mistakes, such as blaming "the model" for something a setting did. The pictures below start with one part and add one more each time.

## 1. The model

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 520 200" role="img" aria-labelledby="gear1-t gear1-d" style="width:100%;height:auto;max-width:520px;font-family:inherit">
<title id="gear1-t">A model with an effort setting</title>
<desc id="gear1-d">One box named model, which reads text and writes text. A dashed box inside it, named effort, shows how much it thinks per step.</desc>
<g stroke-width="2" font-size="16" fill="currentColor">
  <rect x="30" y="50" width="190" height="130" rx="10" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/>
  <text x="46" y="76" font-weight="bold">MODEL</text>
  <text x="46" y="98" font-size="14">reads text, writes text</text>
  <rect x="46" y="116" width="158" height="48" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg);stroke-dasharray:5 3"/>
  <text x="54" y="136" font-size="14">EFFORT: how much</text>
  <text x="56" y="154" font-size="14">it thinks per step</text>
</g>
</svg>
<figcaption>The model reads text and writes text. Effort is a setting on it.</figcaption>
</figure>

- **Model.** The large language model (LLM) that reads and writes text (for example Claude Sonnet 5.5, a Mistral model, or a local model through Ollama, a program that runs models on your own computer). Aliases such as `sonnet` move to newer versions over time, so use the full model name when a result must be reproducible.
- **Effort.** A setting for how much the model reasons before it answers, from `low` to `max` in Claude Code (`/effort`, `--effort`; a `/command` is typed inside the running tool, a `--flag` when you start it). Low is faster and cheaper; high thinks longer and checks more. It steers how much the model reasons per step rather than fixing a number. `max` can show diminishing returns and overthink, so raise it only where you measure a gain.

## 2. The harness

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 520 220" role="img" aria-labelledby="gear2-t gear2-d" style="width:100%;height:auto;max-width:520px;font-family:inherit">
<title id="gear2-t">A model inside a harness</title>
<desc id="gear2-d">A large box named harness contains the model with its effort setting, and three boxes: tools, permissions, and the loop with context.</desc>
<g stroke-width="2" font-size="16" fill="currentColor">
  <rect x="10" y="10" width="500" height="200" rx="14" style="fill:var(--panel);stroke:var(--accent)"/>
  <text x="26" y="36" font-weight="bold" style="fill:var(--accent)">HARNESS</text>
  <rect x="30" y="56" width="190" height="130" rx="10" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/>
  <text x="46" y="82" font-weight="bold">MODEL</text>
  <text x="46" y="104" font-size="14">reads text, writes text</text>
  <rect x="46" y="122" width="158" height="48" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg);stroke-dasharray:5 3"/>
  <text x="54" y="142" font-size="14">EFFORT: how much</text>
  <text x="56" y="160" font-size="14">it thinks per step</text>
  <rect x="260" y="56" width="230" height="38" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="274" y="80">Tools: read, edit, run</text>
  <rect x="260" y="104" width="230" height="38" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="274" y="128">Permissions</text>
  <rect x="260" y="152" width="230" height="38" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="274" y="176">Loop, context</text>
</g>
</svg>
<figcaption>The harness surrounds the model. It supplies tools, applies permissions and runs the loop.</figcaption>
</figure>

- **Harness.** The program around the model. The product you type into is the harness. It provides the tools, manages the context the model sees, runs the loop (gather context, act, check, repeat) and enforces permissions. Claude Code, OpenCode (an open-source harness) and Mistral Vibe (Mistral's open-source terminal coding agent) are harnesses.
- **Tool.** An action the model can request and the harness runs, such as reading a file or running a shell command. A tool call is one such request; tool output is what comes back.
- **Permissions.** The harness's rules for which tool calls it runs, asks about or refuses.
- **Agent.** A model inside a harness that picks and runs tools in a loop toward a goal.

## 3. Extensions

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 520 340" role="img" aria-labelledby="gear3-t gear3-d" style="width:100%;height:auto;max-width:520px;font-family:inherit">
<title id="gear3-t">Extensions plugged into the harness</title>
<desc id="gear3-d">The harness from the previous picture, with a row of extensions: skill, MCP, hook, and an instructions file. A line under skill, MCP and hook marks a plugin as a bundle of them.</desc>
<g stroke-width="2" font-size="16" fill="currentColor">
  <rect x="10" y="10" width="500" height="320" rx="14" style="fill:var(--panel);stroke:var(--accent)"/>
  <text x="26" y="36" font-weight="bold" style="fill:var(--accent)">HARNESS</text>
  <rect x="30" y="56" width="190" height="130" rx="10" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/>
  <text x="46" y="82" font-weight="bold">MODEL</text>
  <text x="46" y="104" font-size="14">reads text, writes text</text>
  <rect x="46" y="122" width="158" height="48" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg);stroke-dasharray:5 3"/>
  <text x="54" y="142" font-size="14">EFFORT: how much</text>
  <text x="56" y="160" font-size="14">it thinks per step</text>
  <rect x="260" y="56" width="230" height="38" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="274" y="80">Tools: read, edit, run</text>
  <rect x="260" y="104" width="230" height="38" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="274" y="128">Permissions</text>
  <rect x="260" y="152" width="230" height="38" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="274" y="176">Loop, context</text>
  <text x="30" y="226" font-weight="bold" style="fill:var(--accent)">EXTENSIONS you plug in</text>
  <rect x="30" y="238" width="90" height="36" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="48" y="261">SKILL</text>
  <rect x="130" y="238" width="90" height="36" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="155" y="261">MCP</text>
  <rect x="230" y="238" width="90" height="36" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="253" y="261">HOOK</text>
  <rect x="330" y="238" width="160" height="36" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg);stroke-dasharray:5 3"/><text x="340" y="261" font-size="14">INSTRUCTIONS FILE</text>
  <path d="M30 292 H320 M30 292 V282 M320 292 V282" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--accent)"/>
  <text x="30" y="314" style="fill:var(--accent)">PLUGIN: a bundle of skills, hooks, MCP</text>
</g>
</svg>
<figcaption>Extensions change what the harness offers. A plugin installs several as one unit.</figcaption>
</figure>

- **Instructions file.** A text file (`CLAUDE.md` in Claude Code, `AGENTS.md` in OpenCode where read) that the harness loads at session start. It advises and does not enforce.
- **Skill.** A folder with a `SKILL.md`. Only its short description is preloaded; the body loads when it is used. It advises.
- **MCP (Model Context Protocol).** An open standard for connecting the harness to outside tools and data, such as a database or a literature search. A server you connect can act on your behalf, so treat it like software you install.
- **Hook.** Your own command, request or prompt that the harness runs automatically at a set point, such as before a tool call. A command hook that exits with code 2 before a tool runs stops that action whatever the model wants (an exit code is the number a script returns; 0 means success, and a hook uses 2 to mean block). A rule in an instructions file can only ask, so hooks are the stronger guard.
- **Plugin.** A folder that bundles skills, hooks, MCP servers and more, installed as one unit. It can run code, so install only plugins you trust.

  <rect x="230" y="238" width="90" height="36" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="253" y="261">HOOK</text>
  <rect x="330" y="238" width="160" height="36" rx="8" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg);stroke-dasharray:5 3"/><text x="340" y="261" font-size="14">INSTRUCTIONS FILE</text>
  <path d="M30 292 H320 M30 292 V282 M320 292 V282" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--accent)"/>
  <text x="30" y="314" style="fill:var(--accent)">PLUGIN: a bundle of skills, hooks, MCP</text>
  <rect x="10" y="350" width="500" height="40" rx="10" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--ok)"/>
  <text x="26" y="375" style="fill:var(--ok)">EVAL: run with and without, compare</text>
</g>
</svg>
<figcaption>An eval sits outside the harness and compares runs.</figcaption>
</figure>

- **Eval.** A repeatable test of agent behaviour: a prompt plus checks on the result. Comparing runs **with** and **without** something (a skill, a rule) shows what it contributed. A score of 100% both ways means the test cannot tell the difference, so make it harder.

## 5. One model, different harnesses

<figure>
<svg viewBox="0 0 520 200" role="img" aria-labelledby="gear5-t gear5-d" style="width:100%;height:auto;max-width:520px;font-family:inherit">
<title id="gear5-t">The same model in two harnesses</title>
<desc id="gear5-d">Two harness boxes side by side, each holding the same model X, each with its own tools, permission rules and loop.</desc>
<g stroke-width="2" font-size="16" fill="currentColor">
  <rect x="10" y="10" width="230" height="170" rx="14" style="fill:var(--panel);stroke:var(--accent)"/>
  <text x="26" y="36" font-weight="bold" style="fill:var(--accent)">HARNESS A</text>
  <rect x="30" y="56" width="190" height="64" rx="10" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="46" y="82">Model X</text>
  <text x="26" y="150" font-size="14">its own tools, rules, loop</text>
  <rect x="270" y="10" width="230" height="170" rx="14" style="fill:var(--panel);stroke:var(--accent)"/>
  <text x="286" y="36" font-weight="bold" style="fill:var(--accent)">HARNESS B</text>
  <rect x="290" y="56" width="190" height="64" rx="10" style="fill:none;stroke:var(--fg)"/><text x="306" y="82">Model X</text>
  <text x="286" y="150" font-size="14">its own tools, rules, loop</text>
</g>
</svg>
<figcaption>Claude Code and OpenCode are two harnesses.</figcaption>
</figure>

The same model can behave differently in each harness, because tools, permission rules and the loop differ. Naming differs between tools too. Check another tool's docs for how its hooks, plugins and effort settings work.

## Other words you will meet

These are not in the pictures.

- **Prompt.** The text you send to the model.
- **Turn.** One prompt from you plus the model's reply.
- **Subagent.** A helper agent with its own context window; only its summary comes back.
- **Sandbox.** An operating-system layer that limits what commands can touch.
- **Hallucination**. A plausible-looking statement that is false, such as an invented DOI (a paper's permanent identifier).
- **Prompt injection.** Text from a file, web page or tool that the model treats as an instruction.

### Words about what the model can see

These get mixed up more than any others.

- **Token.** The chunk of text a model actually reads and writes. Somewhere between a letter and a word. Limits and costs are counted in tokens.
- **Context window.** Everything the model can see at once right now: instructions, files it has read, tool output and the conversation so far. It has a size limit, and a fuller window is not automatically a better one.
- **Session (session context).** One running conversation, and the context window it has built up. A new session starts with an empty conversation. Two sessions do not share their context.
- **Memory.** Notes that the harness loads at the start of every session, such as your instructions file and, in Claude Code, notes the harness writes itself. Memory outlives a session; session context does not.
- **Compaction.** The harness replaces old conversation with a summary to free room.
- **Session usage.** How much of your allowance or bill a session spends. It climbs with the size of the context, because the whole conversation is sent again with each request.
- **Context poisoning.** A community term: a wrong statement gets into the context, and later answers build on it. Start a fresh session and keep unverified claims out of memory files.

<div data-ao-honour="gear-map" data-xp="20">Redraw the picture from memory for the tool you actually use: which model, which harness, which extensions are loaded right now?</div>

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Claude Code overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it is the front page of the docs, a good place to see how much more there is than this course covers.
- [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it is the page that defines the agentic harness and the gather, act, check loop used in this quest.
- [Model configuration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it covers model aliases and the effort setting, so you can pin a model and see what `/effort` changes.
- [Skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it shows the `SKILL.md` format and how only descriptions load at startup.
- [Introduction to the Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro): Model Context Protocol, docs. Why read: it explains what MCP is as an open standard before you connect a server.
- [Define success criteria and build evaluations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it gives the guidance on specific, measurable criteria that evals need.
:::
